joel: Quick heads-up — I saw a regression in streamed responses when continuous batching + partial-decode preemption are enabled. 95p latency for small streams jumped ~30ms in the latest canary. Not sure if it's kernel churn or KV cache churn yet.

maria: ugh, repro steps? which canary?

joel: canary build 2026-03-14-rc3. Repro is small-turn examples (user sends 8-16 tokens, stream enabled). Minimal repro command I used: `./bench_stream --model=redwood-7b --batcher=continuous --seq=256 --stream=true --partial=1 --runs=1000`

akiko: can you paste a short snippet of the perf counters / logs? curious about kernel launch counts vs token count.

joel: pasted a trimmed log below — note the repeated tiny-kernel launches and a spike in L2 misses after partial-decode handoffs:
```
[run 183] batch_id=421 kernel_launches=134 tokens_out=320 partial_preempt=23 kv_miss=18 gpu_ms=14.2
[run 184] batch_id=422 kernel_launches=131 tokens_out=312 partial_preempt=21 kv_miss=20 gpu_ms=13.9
[summary] avg_kernel_per_token=0.41 avg_gpu_ms_per_token=0.044 95p_latency_stream=78ms (baseline 48ms)
```

maria: those kv_miss counts look suspicious for small streaming sends. might be the KV warmup/eviction policy getting triggered on a lot of tiny partials.

shiv: other datapoint — I profiled with CUPTI, saw a ~3x increase in kernel launch overhead (many <1ms kernels). The cost of kernel boundary + small kernel inefficient occupancy seems to dominate for small token outputs.

akiko: could also be admission: token_budget is low so we're preempting aggressively; that increases partial decode churn. What are current admission settings?

joel: canary defaults: token_budget=64, coalesce_window_ms=8, partial_preempt_threshold=0.5, allow_early_send=true

maria: quick mitigation: try bumping token_budget to 128 and coalesce_window_ms to 15 — fewer preemptions should reduce kernel churn and keep KV hot. Worth checking if cost vs latency tradeoff is acceptable.

akiko: agree. also we should try a kernel-routing tweak: when partial_preempt triggers, prefer a 'large-kernel' fallback (coalesced decode) instead of repeatedly launching the tiny per-token kernel. If kernel selection can prefer a denser kernel that runs a handful of extra tokens in one launch, we might cut launch overhead.

shiv: true but that needs patching the kernel selector heuristic — currently it picks kernels by sequence-length bucket per request, not by expected remaining tokens post-preempt. Could add a 'post_partial_lookahead' to consider expected extra tokens and bias to fewer launches.

joel: logged a perf experiment plan in the thread: 1) quick mitigation (config): token_budget=128 + coalesce_window_ms=15 on rc3 canary; 2) profiling run with nvprof/CUPTI to capture kernel counts; 3) a small kernel-selector patch to prefer dense kernel for partial_preempt paths for 3 days A/B test.

infra-bot: Deploy request queued — env=canary-rc3, change-set=#4567 (token_budget tweak). ETA ~6m.

akiko: I'll run the CUPTI trace when the canary is up and post a flamegraph. If we see less kernel launches and fewer KV misses that's a good sign.

maria: also check RT cache heatmap, if warmup still spikes we may need a short KV-holdback for stream-prefetch paths (hold last-used KV pages for Xms after a partial preempt to avoid eviction).

joel: noted. I'll run the mitigation + bench and post numbers. initial hypothesis: majority of regression is kernel launch overhead + tiny KV thrash from frequent partials. If numbers look good, we can ship the config change for the canary and iterate on kernel selection next.

shiv: assign akiko to CUPTI trace, joel to bench runs, maria to KV-heatmap. ping me if you need a quick pairing to sketch the kernel-selection heuristic.

akiko: got it. starting after infra deploy :eyes:  

joel: results (first quick run after config tweak): `95p_latency_stream` fell from 78ms -> 52ms, avg_kernel_per_token dropped 0.41 -> 0.22, kv_miss down by ~60% on small streams. We'll run longer runs and put numbers in a follow-up.

maria: nice — that'll buy us time to design a cleaner kernel-selector + KV holdback.

shiv: next steps in tracker: 1) kernel-selector prototype PR, 2) KV holdback short-duration, 3) longer perf run across larger seqs to ensure no regressions for big batches.

akiko: filing CUPTI trace artifact and brief notes in the ticket.

joel: thanks all. follow-up in #eng-runtime tomorrow 10am to sync if needed. :thumbsup:
